sources.title: Brazil MFA treaty registry: Grenada visa-waiver understanding
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
sources.officialityEvidence: Itamaraty's live official treaty registry identifies the 2014 Brazil-Grenada visa-waiver understanding as in force, entered into force on 9 July 2014, with no expiry or denunciation date.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Vigência: Em Vigor; Data Entrada Vigor: 09/07/2014.

sources.title: Brazil-Grenada reciprocal understanding on visa exemption
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil / Official Gazette
sources.officialityEvidence: The Official Gazette publishes both exchanged notes. Grenada's note expressly exempts Brazilian nationals with valid travel documents for tourism or business, and the current MFA registry records it as in force.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Nacionais da República Federativa do Brasil ... estarão isentos de vistos ... fins de turismo ou visita de negócios.

sources.title: Brazil MFA treaty registry: Tunisia partial visa waiver
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
sources.officialityEvidence: Itamaraty's live official treaty registry records the Brazil-Tunisia partial visa-waiver agreement as in force from 6 August 2004, with no expiry or denunciation date.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Vigência: Em Vigor; Data Entrada Vigor: 06/08/2004.

sources.title: Jordan Tourism Board: visas to Jordan
sources.officialityEvidence: The live official Jordan Tourism Board site publishes a nationality-by-nationality arrival-visa table and explicitly names Brazil.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Brazil | Applicable | Visa can be obtained upon arrival, it will cost a total of 40 JOD.

sources.title: Brazil-Tunisia partial visa-waiver agreement
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
sources.officialityEvidence: The official agreement applies to valid national passports and expressly exempts Brazilian and Tunisian nationals for tourism or business; the MFA registry confirms current force.
sources.supportingExcerpt: portadores de passaportes nacionais válidos, estarão isentos de visto ... fins de turismo ou negócios.

sources.title: Brazil MFA treaty registry: Trinidad and Tobago visa abolition agreement
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
sources.officialityEvidence: Itamaraty's live treaty registry identifies the bilateral agreement on suppression of visas in passports as in force since 7 April 1971, with no expiry or denunciation date.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Acordo sobre a Supressão de Visto em Passaportes ... Vigência: Em Vigor.

sources.title: Brazil MFA treaty registry: Ukraine partial visa waiver
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
sources.officialityEvidence: Itamaraty's live official treaty registry records the Brazil-Ukraine partial visa waiver as in force from 30 October 2011, with no expiry or denunciation date.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Vigência: Em Vigor; Data Entrada Vigor: 30/10/2011.

sources.title: Decree promulgating the Brazil-Ukraine partial visa-waiver agreement
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil / Official Gazette
sources.officialityEvidence: The Official Gazette decree says the agreement entered into force internationally on 30 October 2011; its Article 1 exempts Brazilian and Ukrainian nationals with valid travel documents for tourism and business.
sources.supportingExcerpt: poderão entrar, permanecer, transitar e sair ... sem necessidade de visto, somente para fins de turismo e de negócios.

sources.title: Brazil MFA treaty registry: Saudi visit-visa agreement
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
sources.officialityEvidence: The current registry records an agreement on granting visit visas, not an ordinary-passport visa exemption or a named electronic, arrival or mission issuance timing for Brazilian visitors.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Concessão de Vistos de Visita para Cidadãos de Ambos os Países

sources.title: Djibouti eVisa service
sources.publisher: National Agency for State Information Systems, Republic of Djibouti
sources.officialityEvidence: Djibouti's live state e-government page proves that an approved eVisa is emailed, but it publishes no ordinary Brazilian-passport eligibility or exemption schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Une fois que la demande est approuvée, l'eVisa est envoyé au demandeur par courrier électronique.

sources.title: eVisa South Sudan
sources.publisher: Ministry of Interior, Department of E-Visa and Immigration Service, South Sudan
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Interior Ministry portal describes a pre-travel application but requires applicants to determine eligibility and does not publish a Brazilian ordinary-passport result.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Are you eligible for a South Sudan Visa? Start the application process by creating an account.

sources.title: Liberia Visa on Arrival service
sources.officialityEvidence: Liberia Immigration's live service conditions the arrival route on whether a Liberian embassy is present in the traveler's country, so it does not establish a passport-only Brazilian outcome.
sources.supportingExcerpt: If there is a Liberian embassy in your country, you are required to apply for your visa directly at the embassy.

policies.title: Brazilian ordinary passports: Grenada visa-free short visits
policies.summary: The current Brazil-Grenada reciprocal understanding exempts Brazilian nationals holding valid travel documents for tourism or business visits up to 90 days in 180 days.
conditions: The waiver covers tourism or business visits for no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, using a valid Brazilian travel document; this policy applies that rule to the ordinary Brazilian passport.
Employment, residence, special documents, carrier checks and the destination's individual admission decision remain separate.

policies.title: Brazilian ordinary passports: Tunisia visa-free short visits
policies.summary: The current Brazil-Tunisia agreement exempts holders of valid Brazilian national passports for tourism or business visits up to 90 days, renewable to no more than 180 days annually.
conditions: Use a valid Brazilian national passport for tourism or business. The treaty states up to 90 days, renewable only where the total does not exceed 180 days per year.
Employment, residence, special documents, carrier checks and the destination's individual admission decision remain separate.

policies.title: Brazilian ordinary passports: Jordan visa on arrival
policies.summary: The official Jordan Tourism Board's live nationality table identifies Brazil as eligible to obtain a visa on arrival for 40 JOD.
conditions: Applies to Brazilian ordinary-passport short visitors at Jordanian entry points that issue visas on arrival.
The listed single-entry arrival visa fee is 40 JOD; travellers should complete any current pre-arrival registration requested by Jordan.
This policy does not cover work, residence, special travel documents, or final admission.

policies.title: Brazilian ordinary passports: Trinidad and Tobago visa-free visits
policies.summary: Brazil's current treaty registry and Trinidad and Tobago's Foreign Ministry identify the bilateral Visa Abolition Agreement as operative for passport travel.
conditions: The reviewed current treaty records establish visa abolition for Brazilian passport travel but do not state a visitor-stay maximum in the accessible current material.
Employment, residence, special documents, carrier checks and the destination's individual admission decision remain separate.

policies.title: Brazilian ordinary passports: Ukraine visa-free short visits
policies.summary: The current Brazil-Ukraine treaty registry confirms the operative agreement that exempts Brazilian nationals with valid travel documents for tourism or business visits up to 90 days in 180 days.
conditions: The treaty permits tourism or business entry, transit, stay and exit without a visa for no more than 90 days in a 180-day period from first entry.
The Brazilian travel warning, active hostilities, border accessibility, martial-law measures, special documents, carrier checks and final admission remain separate from this visa classification.
